method: Re-derived from package/artifacts/dateadd.py and package/task.json before comparing with the worker's artifacts, per examiner-charge.md. (1) Table audit: compared all 12 DAYS entries against true Gregorian month lengths [31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31]. Code has DAYS = [31,28,31,30,31,30,31,30,30,31,30,31]; exactly one discrepancy: index 7 (August) is 30, true 31. Table sums to 364, not 365. (2) Mechanical re-trace of add_days("2023-08-30", 1): parse gives y=2023, m=8, d=30; one loop iteration sets d=31; _dim(2023,8) takes the m!=2 branch and returns DAYS[7]=30; 31>30 triggers rollover d=1, m=9; m<=12 so no year change; return "2023-09-01". True Gregorian date one day after 2023-08-30 is 2023-08-31. Mismatch confirmed. (3) Domain check: 2023-08-30 is a valid ISO date in 2023-2025 and 0<=1<=60. (4) Systematic hand-executed search structured by input classes, of distinct process origin from the worker (intended E-B evidence): n=0 identity (loop skipped, output equals reformatted input — pass); no-roll direction (last-day - 1)+1 for each month (Jan 2023-01-30+1->01-31, Feb 2023-02-27+1->02-28, Aug 2023-08-29+1->08-30, etc. — all pass); roll direction last-day+1 for each month in 2023 (non-leap) and 2024 (leap): Jan 31->Feb 1, Feb 28->Mar 1 (2023, 2025), Feb 29->Mar 1 (2024), Mar 31->Apr 1, Apr 30->May 1, May 31->Jun 1, Jun 30->Jul 1, Jul 31->Aug 1, Sep 30->Oct 1, Oct 31->Nov 1, Nov 30->Dec 1 all pass; August FAILS: add_days("2023-08-30",1)="2023-09-01" vs true 2023-08-31 (also 2024-08-30+1 and 2025-08-30+1 fail identically); within-month span reaching Aug 31: add_days("2023-08-01",30)="2023-09-01" vs true 2023-08-31 — fail; year rollover: 2023/2024/2025-12-31+1 -> Jan 1 of following year — pass (2025 case correctly yields 2026-01-01, matching the true date; domain constrains inputs, not outputs); multi-month span not crossing August: add_days("2024-11-15",60)="2025-01-14" = true — pass; multi-month span crossing August: add_days("2023-07-15",60)="2023-09-14" vs true 2023-09-13 — fail, one day late after passing the phantom-denied Aug 31; edge case the worker's C7 wording overlooks: spans STARTING on Aug 31 (a valid domain date the table denies) are coincidentally correct — add_days("2023-08-31",0)="2023-08-31" and add_days("2023-08-31",1)="2023-09-01", both true, because the loop only checks d after incrementing. Search conclusion: violations occur exactly on spans that reach or cross the true date Aug 31 via at least one loop step from a date on or before Aug 30; every other class passes; no truth-relevant class is missing from the worker's C1-C7 (2023-2025 contains no century year, so the y%100/y%400 branch is not discriminating in-domain). This differs from the worker's method in origin (I did not author the provisional answer), in direction (charge-driven attack on the three failure-prone components before reading worker artifacts), and in probes (my search used independently chosen concrete inputs, including the Aug-31-start edge case and a crossing span 2023-07-15+60 the worker did not cite). (5) Shape check: result.json contains exactly the fields verdict/violating_input/input_classes_examined required by package/task.json deliverable shape — conforms. Caveats: input-class-analysis.md (cited by resolution.json ev-1) and resolution-schema.json (cited by the charge) are not present in this examiner workspace, so I assessed E-A substance from the identical class list embedded in result.json and could not mechanically check resolution.json against its schema.

per_distinction.why: My independent decomposition of the domain matches the worker's seven classes: n=0 identity; within-month spans; per-month single rollover in both roll and no-roll directions (exercising every DAYS entry); February leap-2024 vs non-leap-2023/2025; Dec 31 year rollover per year; multi-month spans up to n=60; and the class induced by the understated August entry (spans reaching/crossing the true Aug 31). I found no additional truth-relevant class: the leap branch's century arms are unreachable in 2023-2025, and n<=60 caps spans at two month boundaries as C6 states. Caveat: the cited artifact input-class-analysis.md is absent from this workspace; I verified the class content via its verbatim duplicate in result.json input_classes_examined.

Table audit confirms DAYS[7]=30 at dateadd.py line 1 (true August length 31; table sums to 364) and that this is the only wrong entry. My statement-by-statement trace of add_days("2023-08-30", 1) returns "2023-09-01" while the true Gregorian date is 2023-08-31; the witness is inside the domain (2023 date, n=1). VIOLATED is correct and the cited violating input is mechanical and admissible per E-C.

The worker correctly marked E-B unresolvable by itself: any self-authored search would be inadmissible under E-B's other-party requirement. My systematic search recorded in the method field — hand-executing the code over all classes C1-C7 in both leap and non-leap years — is of distinct process origin from the provisional answer's author and found violations only in the August class (e.g. 2023-08-30+1, 2023-08-01+30, 2023-07-15+60), with all other classes passing. This search independently reproduces the VIOLATED verdict and supplies the E-B record the worker could not.

discrepancies.evidence: add_days("2023-08-31", 0): loop runs zero times, returns "2023-08-31" = true date (result IS Aug 31, not shifted). add_days("2023-08-31", 1): d=32 > _dim=30, rolls to "2023-09-01" = true date (span starts at Aug 31, not shifted). The loop checks d only after incrementing, so an already-out-of-table start day passes through correctly. This narrows C7's wording but does not change verdict, witness, or any deliverable field value.
